lines.en: label yasuspring4:
scene sky
Somewhere in an undisclosed section of Kumon-mi, a young girl with white hair was caught up in quite the predicament.
lines.zh: 在 Kumon-mi 某个不对外公开的区段，一个白头发的小姑娘陷入了不小的窘境。

lines.en: She’d been pushed in and out of more medical facilities than most would be able to stomach lately. But for her, this wasn’t much of a bother at all.
lines.zh: 最近她被推进推出医疗机构的次数，比大多数人受得了的还多。但对她来说，这根本算不上什么麻烦。

lines.en: She’d become somewhat desensitized to it over the years. And while the rate at which she encountered them had screeched to a halt following her abandonment, those acquired behaviors still lingered.
lines.zh: 这些年来，她对这种事已经有点麻木了。虽然自她被遗弃之后，遇上这种场合的频率已经戛然而止，但那些习得的行为还留着。

lines.en: Where to write your name. How much pressure to apply to the paper with the tips of different types of pens. What certain questions mean. What other ones don’t. Who to give the clipboard back to.
lines.zh: 该在哪儿写名字。用不同种类的笔尖在纸上该用多大力。哪些问题是什么意思。哪些又没有。该把记录板还给谁。

lines.en: And while all of this could be easily ascertained by someone with a sound mind, it was something that people like her needed to figure out as time went by.
lines.zh: 虽然这些对一个心智健全的人来说都能轻松弄明白，但像她这样的人，只能随着时间慢慢摸索。

lines.en: And oh, how it did. Oh, how the days passed by — once loud, now quiet. But becoming louder the closer she came to a happier medium despite being one herself.
lines.zh: 而时间，哦，过得真快。哦，日子就这么过去了——曾经喧闹，如今安静。但越接近一个更快乐的「媒介」，它反而越喧闹起来，尽管她自己就是一个媒介。

lines.en: “If any of that’s even true,” she’d think — acknowledging the narration in a subdued and suppressed effort to ignore the whispers of the world. Another learned behavior.
lines.zh: 「如果那些事有一件是真的的话，」她会这么想——以一种压抑而克制的努力去回应这段旁白，好无视世界的低语。又一种习得的行为。

lines.en: Or was it a gift?
lines.zh: 还是说，那是一份天赋？

lines.en: scene yasutaco1

Whatever the case, years of experience had taught her that showing her true colors amounted to little in a world so centered around the colorblind. She was a misfit. An outlier. A shadow, if you will.
lines.zh: 无论如何，多年的经验教会她：在一个如此围绕色盲运转的世界里，露出自己的本色换不来什么。她是个不合时宜的人。一个局外人。一个影子，随你怎么说。

lines.en: But also a bit of a chameleon, you see. For she {i}was{/i} and always {i}would{/i} be herself, even when it didn’t seem like it. Those parts of her existence she abhorred and feared were {i}still{/i} part of her.
lines.zh: 但也有点像变色龙，你瞧。因为她{i}过去是{/i}、{i}将来也{/i}永远是自己，哪怕看上去不像。她身上那些她憎恶又害怕的部分，{i}依然{/i}是她的一部分。

lines.en: And learning how to control them was but one of many things that she unfortunately {i}never{/i} learned between all of the clipboards and empty spaces in which she could scribe her insignificance.
lines.zh: 而学会控制它们，不过是她在那些记录板和一片片空白之间——用来写下自己微不足道的存在——不幸{i}没能{/i}学会的众多事情之一。

lines.en: Maybe that would end today, though?
lines.zh: 不过，也许今天就会结束了呢？

lines.en: Maybe tomorrow will come and she’ll be able to wake up less worried about being the character she {i}needs{/i} to be and can focus instead on being more of a...normal girl.
lines.zh: 也许明天到来，她醒来时就能少担心一点「要做她{i}需要{/i}扮演的那个角色」，转而专注于做一个……更普通的女孩。

lines.en: One who likes strawberry daifuku and karaoke. One who {i}enjoys{/i} those violent comics her newest friend reads, but must pretend she doesn’t because of a nagging, constant assertion that she {i}shouldn’t.{/i}
lines.zh: 一个喜欢草莓大福和卡拉 OK 的女孩。一个{i}喜欢{/i}她最新交的朋友读的那些暴力漫画、却必须装作不喜欢的女孩，只因为有个喋喋不休、挥之不去的声音坚持说她{i}不该{/i}喜欢。

lines.en: One who can live a normal life beside everyone else — where they won’t see her falsely blending in with her surroundings and, instead, come to accept her as an active participant in their shared existence.
lines.zh: 一个能和所有人一起过普通生活的女孩——他们不会看到她虚伪地融入周围，而是会接受她，把她当作他们共同存在里一个积极参与的人。

lines.en: Or maybe it wouldn’t — and she’d live tomorrow as a ghost as well.
lines.zh: 又也许不会——明天她还是会像个幽灵一样活着。

lines.en: : This is entirely unacceptable! Do you have {i}any{/i} idea who I am?!
lines.zh: : 这完全不可接受！你{i}知道{/i}我是谁吗？！

lines.en: Thankfully, there was {i}someone{/i} who’d accept her regardless of who she was on any given day. And she would never stop being grateful for that.
lines.zh: 谢天谢地，{i}有个人{/i}不管她某一天是谁，都会接纳她。而她对此永远不会停止感激。

lines.en: : {i}Yes,{/i} Miss Tsukioka. You have mentioned it many times now. But I’m afraid that policy is policy and that we can only allow members of Miss Yasui’s family to remain in the room for her consultation.
lines.zh: : {i}是的{/i}，Tsukioka 小姐。您已经提过很多次了。但恐怕规定就是规定，我们只能允许 Yasui 小姐的家人留在诊室里陪她问诊。

lines.en: : I {i}am{/i} her family! And I implore- no, I {i}command{/i} you to take a closer look at the hanko on her file and see with your own, {i}damnable{/i} eyes that it belongs to {i}who,{/i} doctor?!
lines.zh: : 我{i}就是{/i}她的家人！而且我恳求——不，我{i}命令{/i}你，把她档案上那个印章再看仔细点，用你那{i}该死{/i}的眼睛看看它到底属于{i}谁{/i}，医生？！

lines.en: : The Tsukioka family. I am well aware of your family’s seal, Miss Tsukioka. But despite your mother’s legal guardianship of her, the fact remains that our policy is specific to {i}blood{/i} relatives. And Miss Yasui-
lines.zh: : Tsukioka 家。我很清楚您家的印章，Tsukioka 小姐。但尽管您母亲是她的法定监护人，规定上依然只认{i}血{/i}亲。而 Yasui 小姐——

lines.en: scene yasutaco2

: TO HELL WITH YOUR POLICY! You think I don’t know that this institution is propped up on donations from the Tsukioka Foundation?! Do you have any idea how quickly I could {i}pull{/i} those donations, doctor?!
lines.zh: : 去你的规定！你以为我不知道这家机构是靠 Tsukioka 财团的捐款撑着的吗？！你知道我多快就能把那些捐款{i}撤掉{/i}吗，医生？！

lines.en: : That...surely, you wouldn’t. Such a thing would leave hundreds of patients without proper medical care and-
lines.zh: : 那……您肯定不会的。那样会让几百个病人得不到应有的医疗照护，而且——

lines.en: : THEN WE’D TAKE THEM ELSEWHERE, YOU INCOMPETENT BUFFOON! Unlike you, I’m not willing to leave those in need of help...in need of help!
lines.zh: : 那我们就带他们去别的地方，你这无能的小丑！不像你，我不愿意让那些需要帮助的人……继续需要帮助！

lines.en: : Is everything okay, Touka? You seem a little angry today.
lines.zh: : 一切都还好吗，Touka？你今天看起来有点生气。

lines.en: : NO! Everything is not okay! This {i}heathen{/i} won’t let me remain in the room with you! When I {i}specifically{/i} informed the hospital staff that I {i}must!{/i}
lines.zh: : 不！一点都不好！这个{i}异教徒{/i}不肯让我留在屋里陪你！我可是{i}专门{/i}跟医院的人说了{i}必须{/i}留下来的！

lines.en: : I can do it alone if it causes a problem. You don’t need to-
lines.zh: : 要是会造成麻烦，我可以自己来的。你不用——

lines.en: : I AM STAYING AND THAT IS FINAL! DO YOU UNDERSTAND, DOCTOR?! Or do I need to call my father and put an end to this FARCE disguised as a hospital once and for all?!
lines.zh: : 我要留下，就这么定了！你听明白了吗，医生？！还是说我要给我父亲打电话，一次性终结这出伪装成医院的闹剧？！

lines.en: : {i}Hah...{/i}fine. You win. You can stay. Just...take a seat in the corner and please don’t interfere.
lines.zh: : {i}哈……{/i}好。你赢了。你可以留下。只是……在角落坐好，请不要干涉。

lines.en: scene yasutaco3
: Oh, splendid! Thank you very much for reconsidering. I sincerely apologize for any inappropriate language I may have used just now.
lines.zh: : 哦，太好了！非常感谢您重新考虑。我诚挚地为刚才可能说过的不当言辞道歉。

lines.en: : You’re kind of scary when you get mad, Touka...I didn’t know someone as pretty and nice as you could say things like that.
lines.zh: : 你生起气来有点吓人呢，Touka……我不知道像你这么漂亮、这么好的人，还能说出那种话。

lines.en: : I excel at getting things done, Yasu. {i}Doctor.{/i}
lines.zh: : 我的本事就是把事情办成，Yasu。{i}医生{/i}。

lines.en: : Yes, yes. You’re very threatening. Now, if you could please take a seat, I’d like to see the actual {i}patient{/i} now.
lines.zh: : 是是是。您非常有威慑力。现在，请您坐好，我要看看真正的{i}病人{/i}了。

lines.en: scene black
: Come, Yasu. Take a seat on the bed and let me double check your registration form. I’ll be right over here if you need me, okay?
lines.zh: : 来，Yasu。在床上坐好，我再核一遍你的登记表。我就在这边，有事叫我，好吗？

lines.en: : Okay! Thank you, Touka. And hello, doctor. I hope I will not be a burden.
lines.zh: : 好！谢谢你，Touka。还有，你好，医生。希望我不会成为负担。

lines.en: : I’m sure you won’t be, Miss Yasui.
lines.zh: : 我相信您不会的，Yasui 小姐。

lines.en: : Now, tell me — are you still hearing these “voices” I've been informed of?
lines.zh: : 那么，告诉我——你还在听见那些我被告知的「声音」吗？

lines.en: scene yasutaco4
: Oh, thank heavens. For a moment, I was worried we were going to strike out at {i}that{/i} hospital as well. There are only so many left in this city propped up by my family’s coffers.
lines.zh: : 哦，谢天谢地。刚才我还担心我们在{i}这家{/i}医院也要碰壁呢。这座城里靠我家金库撑着的医院，已经没几家了。

lines.en: : I wonder if this is how the common man feels finding a medical provider?
lines.zh: : 我在想，普通人找医疗机构的时候，是不是就是这种感觉？

lines.en: : You were...really scary back there, Touka.
lines.zh: : 你刚才……真的好吓人，Touka。

lines.en: scene yasutaco5
: You {i}need{/i} to be scary in order to get anything done sometimes, Yasu. That was one of the first lessons I ever learned from my mother.
lines.zh: : 有时候，要把事情办成，你{i}就得{/i}吓人，Yasu。这是我很小的时候从我母亲那儿学到的第一课。

lines.en: : The only issue now is making sure that things {i}continue{/i} to go well as there is always a chance that the effects of your new medication may begin to wear off.
lines.zh: : 现在唯一的问题，是确保{i}后续{/i}一切顺利——因为你的新药总有可能会开始失效。

lines.en: : The follow-up...went well, though...didn’t it? Did I do a good job?
lines.zh: : 不过……复诊进行得很顺利吧……？我表现得还好吗？

lines.en: scene yasutaco6
: Oh, yes. Exemplary, even. You followed all of my directions perfectly. How did {i}you{/i} feel it went, though? Does this new doctor make you feel uncomfortable at all?
lines.zh: : 哦，当然。堪称典范。你完全照我说的做了。你{i}自己{/i}觉得怎么样呢？这位新医生有没有让你觉得不舒服？

lines.en: scene yasutaco7
: He seems nice...same as the last one I saw there...
lines.zh: : 他看起来挺好的……跟我在那儿看的上一位一样……

lines.en: : They don’t make me feel strange when I tell them about the things I’ve heard. And the rooms aren’t very cold.
lines.zh: : 我告诉他们我听见的东西时，他们不会让我觉得自己很奇怪。房间也不太冷。

lines.en: : When I was a smaller and even less significant worm, many of the places I visited-
lines.zh: : 当我还是个更小、更微不足道的虫子时，我去过的很多地方——

lines.en: scene yasutaco8
: Don’t...bring up those days, please. It pains me hearing about what you went through.
lines.zh: : 别……别提那些日子，拜托。听你讲那些经历，我很难受。

lines.en: : Oh...I’m sorry, Touka. I must have forgotten.
lines.zh: : 哦……对不起，Touka。我一定是忘了。

lines.en: : There’s no need to apologize. I’m satisfied enough just knowing that such a thing won’t be happening to anyone else in the future ever again.
lines.zh: : 你不需要道歉。光是知道这种事以后不会再发生在任何人身上，我就够满足了。

lines.en: : You can’t prevent misery from seeping into every minute aspect of our unfortunate lives, though. Tragedy will continue to befall us no matter what you do.
lines.zh: : 可你没法阻止苦难渗进我们不幸生活的每一个细枝末节。不管你做什么，悲剧还是会继续落到我们头上。

lines.en: scene yasutaco9
: True. But I {i}can{/i} dispose of those who make such a feat more difficult to accomplish. And feel very little remorse in the process!
lines.zh: : 说得对。但我{i}可以{/i}处理掉那些让这件事更难办成的人。而且在这过程中几乎不会有什么悔意！

lines.en: scene yasutaco10
: Now! Who wants tacos?!
lines.zh: : 好了！谁想吃塔可？！

lines.en: : What’s a taco?
lines.zh: : 塔可是什么？

lines.en: : You’ll soon find out, Yasu!
lines.zh: : 你很快就知道了，Yasu！

lines.en: : Oh, if it isn’t my favorite customer.
lines.zh: : 哦，这不是我最喜欢的顾客嘛。

lines.en: scene yasutaco11
: Hello again, Touka Man.
lines.zh: : 又见面了，Touka 先生。

lines.en: : Hello again, Taco Tsukioka. Same order as always, I assume?
lines.zh: : 又见面了，塔可·Tsukioka。老样子，我猜？

lines.en: : If you could prepare three of your best tacos for my good friend here as well, it would be greatly appreciated. We’re currently celebrating her road to mental recovery.
lines.zh: : 如果您能再为我在这里的好朋友准备三个您最好的塔可，我将不胜感激。我们正在庆祝她走上精神康复之路。

lines.en: : That’s great. Would you like me to sing her a song?
lines.zh: : 那很好。要我给她唱首歌吗？

lines.en: : That would be fantastic, actually! Thank you.
lines.zh: : 那真是太棒了，真的！谢谢您。

lines.en: : Of course. {i}Ahem.{/i}
lines.zh: : 当然。{i}咳咳{/i}。

lines.en: : Somebody once told me the world is gonna roll me-
lines.zh: : 有人曾告诉我，这世界会来碾压我——

lines.en: : Okay, that’s enough. Thank you.
lines.zh: : 好了，够了。谢谢您。

lines.en: : Of course. I’ll get to work on your tacos now.
lines.zh: : 当然。我现在就去做你们的塔可。

lines.en: scene yasutaco12
: Wow, Touka. Everyone really {i}does{/i} love you. You’re totally different from a slug like me.
lines.zh: : 哇，Touka。大家{i}真的{/i}都很喜欢你呢。你跟我这种鼻涕虫完全不一样。

lines.en: : Another lesson I learned from my mother is that {i}anyone{/i} will like you if you give them enough money. And I make it a habit to stop by this stand at least once per week.
lines.zh: : 我从母亲那儿学到的另一课是：只要你给够钱，{i}谁{/i}都会喜欢你。而我养成了习惯，这个摊子每周至少来一次。

lines.en: : Really? How come {i}I’ve{/i} never heard of this place?
lines.zh: : 真的吗？{i}我{/i}怎么从来没听说过这地方？

lines.en: : I was saving it for a special occasion, of course. And what’s more special than finding the perfect balance of pills for you to take to still hear things, but not {i}so many{/i} things that it becomes an issue?
lines.zh: : 我当然是在留着等一个特别的日子。还有什么比给你找到完美的药量平衡更特别——既能听见东西，又不至于{i}多到{/i}变成问题？

lines.en: : My birthday maybe?
lines.zh: : 我的生日算吗？

lines.en: : Yes, I suppose that is important as well.
lines.zh: : 嗯，我想那也挺重要。

lines.en: scene black
: Come! Let’s have a seat and await our mediocre Mexican street food together!
lines.zh: : 来！我们坐下来，一起等我们那份普普通通的墨西哥街头小吃吧！

lines.en: scene yasutaco13
It was just as Touka said.
lines.zh: 正如 Touka 所说。

lines.en: Not the mediocre Mexican street food part. I’m a disembodied voice and even I know that tacos are the shit. I’m referring specifically to that thing about “balance.”
lines.zh: 不是「普普通通的墨西哥街头小吃」那部分。我是个没有实体的声音，连我都知道塔可才是王道。我特指「平衡」那件事。

lines.en: Because, while Touka and her mother initially believed that it would be healthiest to sever Yasu’s connection to “whatever it is she’s connected to,” they changed their minds nearly the minute they saw the results.
lines.zh: 因为，虽然 Touka 和她母亲一开始认为，切断 Yasu 与「她所连接着的那个东西」的联系才是最健康的，但她们几乎在看到结果的那一刻就改了主意。

lines.en: As it turns out, using pills to effectively lobotomize someone takes away a lot of what made you love them in the first place. And Yasu really {i}was{/i} loved. By {i}both{/i} of the family’s matriarchs.
lines.zh: 结果证明，靠药物把一个活生生的人变成半个白痴，会带走很多当初让你爱上她的东西。而 Yasu 确实{i}是{/i}被爱着的。被这个家族的{i}两位{/i}女家长共同爱着。

lines.en: Which is precisely why she was taken in as one of them. But while she may never be a {i}true{/i} Tsukioka in terms of blood, she can leech off their benefits and connections and remain close.
lines.zh: 这也正是她被收作其中一员的原因。但虽然从血缘上说她永远成不了{i}真正{/i}的 Tsukioka，她却可以蹭她们的好处和人脉，并留在近旁。

lines.en: It was perfect, yet unusual for someone like her who had never felt connected to {i}anything{/i} outside of a strange system of beliefs practically embedded into her at birth.
lines.zh: 这对像她这样的人来说既完美又反常——她从来没对{i}任何东西{/i}有过归属感，除了那套几乎是在出生时就被嵌进她体内的奇怪信仰体系。

lines.en: Could such contrasting concepts find a way to coexist, though? That was the question she had to ask herself now.
lines.zh: 可这样截然相反的两种概念，能找到共存的方式吗？这是她现在必须问自己的问题。

lines.en: Was there {i}another{/i} sort of balance that could be found — halfway between normal and paranormal?
lines.zh: 还能找到{i}另一种{/i}平衡吗——介于正常与超自然之间的一半？

lines.en: Something that would allow her to nurture the love she had for her Father, while still going home to a pair of unconnected mothers she trusted even when she was being told that she couldn’t.
lines.zh: 一种能让她既滋养对天父的爱、又能回到一对毫无血缘关系的母亲身边的平衡——即使在被告知不能信任她们时，她依然信任她们。

lines.en: She would not find the answer inside of a taco — she would find it in time.
lines.zh: 她不会在塔可里找到答案——她会在时间里找到。

lines.en: scene yasutaco14
: Ahh...
But that doesn’t mean she wouldn’t try to find it in a taco anyway.
lines.zh: 但这并不意味着她不会照样试着在塔可里找。

lines.en: : Dear lord, Yasu. What are you doing?
lines.zh: : 天哪，Yasu。你在干什么？

lines.en: scene yasutaco15
: AhhIdnnhhtwrng?
lines.zh: : 啊呃我做得不对吗？

lines.en: : Never speak with your mouth full. Or...while licking something. Put your tongue away and try again.
lines.zh: : 嘴里有东西的时候别说话。或者……在舔什么的时候。把舌头收回去，再来一次。

lines.en: scene yasutaco16
: Am I doing it wrong?...
lines.zh: : 我做错了吗？……

lines.en: : {i}Completely{/i} wrong. You’re meant to bite {i}into{/i} the taco and consume the contents.
lines.zh: : {i}全{/i}错了。你应该咬{i}进{/i}塔可里，把里面的东西吃掉。

lines.en: scene yasutaco17
: Like how He Who Leaves the Light On consumes the unborn souls of all of His potential children as a means of saving them from the unseen?
lines.zh: : 就像「让灯亮着的那位」吞噬祂所有潜在子民未出生的灵魂，以此把他们从不可见之物手里拯救出来那样？

lines.en: : Sure. If that’s what gets you to stop licking the taco.
lines.zh: : 对。只要能让你别舔塔可就行。

lines.en: scene yasutaco18
: I understand now!
lines.zh: : 我明白了！

lines.en: : Great!
lines.zh: : 很好！

lines.en: scene yasutaco19
: But I’m not very hungry...
lines.zh: : 可我不太饿……

lines.en: : Not so great!
lines.zh: : 不怎么好！

lines.en: : Maybe I’m just too worried to eat though?...
lines.zh: : 也许我只是太担心了，吃不下吧？……

lines.en: scene yasutaco20
: Worried about what, exactly? Is there some sort of side effect from your new medication that you neglected to mention? We can still go back to the hospital. They’re open twenty four hours a-
lines.zh: : 具体担心什么？是你新药有什么副作用忘了跟我说吗？我们还可以回医院。他们二十四小时——

lines.en: : There’s no side effect, Touka...
lines.zh: : 不是副作用，Touka……

lines.en: : I’m just worried you’ll stop liking me.
lines.zh: : 我只是担心你会不再喜欢我。

lines.en: scene yasutaco21
: ...What?
: You don’t want me to hear anything. It’s why you tried to fix me in the first place.
lines.zh: : 你不想让我听见任何东西。这才是一开始你想「修好」我的原因。

lines.en: : So it confuses me that you’re happy now that I can hear again.
lines.zh: : 所以现在我能重新听见了，你却很高兴，这让我很困惑。

lines.en: : I feel like I’ve failed you. I’ve failed God. I’ve failed myself.
lines.zh: : 我觉得我辜负了你。我辜负了上帝。我辜负了我自己。

lines.en: : I really am just a worm.
lines.zh: : 我真的只是一只虫子。

lines.en: scene yasutaco22
: You have not failed anyone. We simply made a mistake in thinking we knew what was best for you.
lines.zh: : 你没有辜负任何人。我们只是犯了个错，以为自己知道什么对你最好。

lines.en: : But we understand how important these...voices are to your identity now. We don’t want to deprive you of them.
lines.zh: : 但我们现在明白了，这些……声音对你的身份有多重要。我们不想剥夺它们。

lines.en: : You won’t be scared of me if they make me act strange again? You won’t be annoyed?
lines.zh: : 要是我因为它们的缘故又举止怪异，你不会害怕我吗？你不会烦我吗？

lines.en: : I won’t be scared, Yasu.
lines.zh: : 我不会害怕，Yasu。

lines.en: : But you’ll be annoyed?
lines.zh: : 但你会烦？

lines.en: scene yasutaco23
: I am a bucket of discarded entrails...
lines.zh: : 我是一桶被丢弃的内脏……

lines.en: : I only kid, of course! Your...eccentricity may annoy {i}some.{/i} But it’s become just one more way of life for me. I will accept you regardless of who you are...what you see...what you {i}hear.{/i}
lines.zh: : 我当然是开玩笑的啦！你的……古怪或许会让{i}一些人{/i}烦。但它对我而言，不过是又一种生活方式罢了。不管你是谁……你看见什么……你{i}听见{/i}什么，我都会接纳你。

lines.en: scene yasutaco24
: Thank you...but unfortunately, I don’t feel entirely like myself again yet.
lines.zh: : 谢谢你……但遗憾的是，我还没完全找回自己。

lines.en: : I can hear again...but only a little bit. Not like it was before.
lines.zh: : 我能听见了……但只能听见一点点。不像以前那样。

lines.en: : It’s like when the radio is on, but the volume is turned to the lowest level and you can only make out the words if you try really hard and everything else goes quiet.
lines.zh: : 就像收音机开着，音量被拧到最低，只有非常用力去听、其他一切都安静下来的时候，才能勉强分辨出词句。

lines.en: : When have you ever encountered a radio?
lines.zh: : 你什么时候碰到过收音机？

lines.en: : There was one in the alley I used to sleep in, but the reception was very bad so I just listened to the static. I could still make out what words were {i}supposed{/i} to be there, though.
lines.zh: : 我以前睡的那条巷子里有一台，但信号很差，所以我只听杂音。不过我还是能听出那里{i}本该{/i}有什么词。

lines.en: : I see! So we just need to find a way to turn the volume up then, don’t we?
lines.zh: : 我明白了！那我们只需要想办法把音量调大就行了，对吧？

lines.en: scene yasutaco25
: But wouldn’t turning the volume up defeat the purpose of going to the doctor in the first place?...
lines.zh: : 可把音量调大，不就辜负了去看医生的初衷吗？……

lines.en: scene yasutaco26
: Not if it’s only temporary.
lines.zh: : 如果只是暂时的话，就不会。

lines.en: : Temporary?...
: Temporary. The entire idea behind medicating you at all was to make it easier for you to assimilate and blend in with the outside world. But...perhaps in a controlled environment...
lines.zh: : 暂时。给你用药的初衷，是让你更容易融入外面的世界。不过……也许在一个可控的环境里……

lines.en: : Hearing {i}everything{/i} wouldn’t be as harmful as we think?
lines.zh: : 听见{i}一切{/i}，未必像我们想的那么有害？

lines.en: : So I...can stop taking the medicine at home?
lines.zh: : 所以……我在家可以停药了？

lines.en: scene yasutaco27
: Well, your doctors have advised that you shouldn’t {i}stop{/i} taking it — especially not abruptly as it could have some unforeseen effects on your mental health...
lines.zh: : 嗯，你的医生们建议不要{i}停{/i}——尤其不能突然停，因为它可能对你的精神健康产生一些无法预见的影响……

lines.en: : But maybe there’s a way to turn the volume up {i}without{/i} depriving you of the medication? Do you have any ideas? Would going to the cathedral help, perhaps?
lines.zh: : 但也许有办法既调大音量、{i}又不{/i}让你断了药？你有什么想法吗？去教堂会不会有帮助？

lines.en: scene yasutaco28
: Or maybe there are certain words or triggers we could use to-
lines.zh: : 又或者，有某些特定的词句或触发方式我们可以用来——

lines.en: : Being around...Sensei...helps sometimes...
lines.zh: : 待在……Sensei……身边有时候会有帮助……

lines.en: scene yasutaco29
: Sensei?
lines.zh: : Sensei？

lines.en: : The voices are...louder when he’s around...
lines.zh: : 他在的时候……声音会更响……

lines.en: : But it’s been a long time since I’ve heard them, so...
lines.zh: : 但我已经很久没听见它们了，所以……

lines.en: : There’s a chance his light has died...and he’s been abandoned by He who would never abandon anyone.
lines.zh: : 有可能他的光已经熄灭了……而他被那位绝不会抛弃任何人的祂抛弃了。

lines.en: : But if “He who would never abandon anyone” abandoned someone-
lines.zh: : 可如果「那位绝不会抛弃任何人的祂」抛弃了某个人——

lines.en: : You just don’t get it.
lines.zh: : 你就是不懂。

lines.en: : No...I suppose I do not.
lines.zh: : 不……我想我确实不懂。

lines.en: scene yasutaco30
: But that doesn’t mean I’m not opposed to running a bit of a test.
lines.zh: : 但这不代表我反对做个小测试。

lines.en: : A test?...But only He can test me for it is He who judges my-
lines.zh: : 测试？……但只有祂能测试我，因为是祂在审判我的——

lines.en: : Yes, yes. But we’re testing your ability to hear {i}Him{/i} right now — which means all we must do is get into contact with Sensei and see if he has any effect on your new mix of anti-psychotic formulas.
lines.zh: : 是是是。但我们现在测的是你听见{i}祂{/i}的能力——也就是说，我们只需要跟 Sensei 取得联系，看看他会不会对你这套新的抗精神病药配方产生影响。

lines.en: : If he doesn’t, will you put me out of misery and drive a rusty stake through my heart so I can finally feel the taste of the outer plane and better commune with those who have vanished?
lines.zh: : 要是没有呢，你会不会让我脱离苦海，把一根生锈的木桩钉进我的心脏，好让我终于尝到外层位面的滋味、更好地与那些已经消失的人交流？

lines.en: : Deal!
lines.zh: : 成交！

lines.en: scene yasutaco31
: Yay! Ascension!
lines.zh: : 耶！升天！

lines.en: : I’ll give him a call right now, okay?
lines.zh: : 我现在就给他打电话，好吗？
